reviewed_source_mapping.contract_gate: Keep the page mapping partial. Importing WebSocket from fastapi to run the workload does not assert import-path or object identity, and none of these selectors records Python signatures. The case does not exercise the listed scope, connection-property, or state members; WebSocketDisconnect raising/catching on a client disconnect; WebSocketState values or transitions; bytes or JSON helpers; iterators; raw receive/send; accept subprotocol/headers; close reasons; denial responses; or invalid state transitions. The client disconnect supplied by the recipe is not consumed by the endpoint after it closes, so it is not evidence for WebSocketDisconnect behavior. The documented HTTPConnection tip has a separate reference-page mapping and is not counted as this page's linked case.
reviewed_source_mapping.rationale: FastAPI 0.141.1 exposes Starlette's WebSocket and WebSocketDisconnect through fastapi.websockets and re-exports those two names at the fastapi root; WebSocketState is available from fastapi.websockets, not the root. FastAPI owns @app.websocket registration, APIWebSocketRoute construction, and typed WebSocket/HTTPConnection dependency injection. Starlette 1.6.0 owns the WebSocket class, its state machine and helper methods, WebSocketDisconnect and WebSocketState, inherited HTTPConnection properties, and generic WebSocket route dispatch. The page-linked input samples one endpoint session, not the referenced class API as a whole.

reviewed_mapping.contract_gate: Keep this function partial. The new direct-ASGI case observes status, the full ordered raw response headers including Set-Cookie, and exact body bytes, but its independently authored message and cookie values differ from the upstream app. Complete header equality and body bytes are stricter than the source's response.cookies value lookup and response.json() semantic equality; http.body.json remains workflow-planned. Raw Set-Cookie bytes do not establish the source's `response.cookies["fakesession"]` assertion: Starlette TestClient creates an HTTPX Response and delegates post() through httpx.Client, so cookie-jar projection is client behavior outside this ASGI workflow. The separate http.cookies selector is also planned and would represent parsed Set-Cookie records, not HTTPX jar lookup semantics.
reviewed_mapping.rationale: The source asserts status 200, parsed JSON equality, and a value retrieved from the HTTPX response cookie jar after the route directly returns JSONResponse. FastAPI owns the direct-Response dispatch branch. Starlette 1.6.0 owns JSONResponse rendering, set_cookie header construction, and ASGI emission; FastAPI's TestClient name is a re-export of Starlette's HTTPX-backed client.

reviewed_mapping.contract_gate: The new ASGI workflow exercises this route-level request-to-encoder-to-Response composition using an independently named /inventory/{sku} route and InventoryItem model, not an exact replay of the source /items/{id} app. Exact body bytes and ordered headers are stricter than the upstream status and response.json() assertions; the source does not assert headers or wire formatting. The upstream TestClient.put(json=...) request encoding and HTTPX Response.json() decoding remain client-only assertions outside the direct-ASGI workflow.
reviewed_mapping.rationale: The test sends a Pydantic body model to a PUT route, explicitly converts the model with FastAPI's jsonable_encoder, returns JSONResponse, and asserts the status and decoded body. The independent workflow additionally observes response headers and body bytes. FastAPI owns request resolution and the direct-Response branch; JSONResponse rendering and ASGI framing are Starlette behavior.
